preconditions.description: The number of nodes n is between 2 and 10^5 inclusive.
There are exactly n-1 edges provided, forming a tree structure.

preconditions.expression: all(1 <= u <= n and 1 <= v <= n and u != v for u, v, x, c in edges)
preconditions.description: Each edge connects two distinct nodes within the valid range [1, n].

preconditions.expression: all(1 <= x <= 1000000006 for u, v, x, c in edges)
preconditions.description: The clamminess value x for each edge is between 1 and 10^9 + 6 inclusive.

preconditions.expression: all(c in (0, 1) for u, v, x, c in edges)
preconditions.description: The color c for each edge is either 0 (red) or 1 (black).

postconditions.description: The output is a single integer string representing the computed jelliness modulo 10^9 + 7.
The result is the product of clamminess values of all valid paths modulo 10^9 + 7, or 1 if no valid paths exist.

postconditions.expression: valid_paths == [path_product for u, v in all_pairs if abs(red_count(u, v) - black_count(u, v)) <= 2]
postconditions.description: A path is valid if the absolute difference between the count of red threads (color 0) and black threads (color 1) on the unique path between nodes u and v is at most 2. The path_product is the product of clamminess values of edges on that path.

postconditions.expression: all_pairs == [(u, v) for u in range(1, n + 1) for v in range(u + 1, n + 1)]
postconditions.description: The set of pairs considered includes every unique pair of distinct nodes exactly once, regardless of direction.
